summary.text: 开 means “open” and “begin.” It is the standardized simplified form of 開, created by omitting 門. The older graph’s construction is disputed; the familiar hands-and-latch explanation is not a settled account of its origin.

formation.text: 开 is derived from 開 by standard simplification. For 開, the received analysis names 門 and 幵, while another historical analysis treats 幵 as a sound element. The popular hands-and-latch account remains an interpretation rather than an established original formation.

components.text: This graph is the standardized simplified form of 開, with 門 omitted. Its visible strokes are not analyzed here as separate historical components.

history.text: The 1956 simplification scheme pairs 开 with 開. In the simplified graph, 門 is omitted; this graphic change does not resolve competing analyses of the older graph.

uncertainties.text: The received Shuowen analysis treats 門 and 幵 as components, while Duan Yucai treats 幵 as phonetic. A separate paleographic argument proposes 幵 as an earlier graph for the word. These accounts leave the older graph’s construction unsettled.

senses.text: 开 means “open”; the earliest occurrence is not dated here.
开 also means “begin,” “initiate,” or “start.” Its chronological relation to “open” is unresolved.
The received Shuowen entry glosses 開 as “stretch/open.” This is a historical dictionary interpretation, not a dated first meaning.
A paleographic argument proposes these as early uses of 開 and suggests 啟 was more common for opening doors. This proposal does not establish a settled chronology.

limitations.text: No dated progression among “stretch/open,” “open,” “begin,” or the proposed instructing, explaining, and releasing senses is established, so no semantic development is asserted.

No glyph image can be selected because the available research did not verify any candidate image’s identity and provenance for 開. The Xiaoxuetang page exposed no character-specific image, and the located Commons image depicts another character.
